canonical.name: The circle as $S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ with basepoint $[0]$
Agreement with the published quotient model of $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$
The quotient map is open, and every interval shorter than one embeds in $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$
$p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ is a covering map with translated interval sheets
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ is compact and path-connected
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ is Hausdorff
The standard circle loops $\omega_n(t)=[nt]$ for $n\in\mathbb Z$
The degree of a based circle loop
Path-homotopic based circle loops have the same degree
Degree defines a function $\operatorname{Deg}:\pi_1(S^1,[0])\to\mathbb Z$
$\deg(\omega_n)=n$ for every integer $n$
Lifts of circle-loop concatenations and reversals
Degree sends concatenation to addition, reversal to negation, and the constant loop to zero
$\operatorname{Deg}:\pi_1(S^1,[0])\to(\mathbb Z,+)$ is a group homomorphism
Based circle loops of equal degree are path-homotopic
Two based circle loops are path-homotopic if and only if they have equal degree
A based circle loop is nullhomotopic exactly when its degree is zero
$\operatorname{Deg}:\pi_1(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z,[0])\to(\mathbb Z,+)$ is an isomorphism
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ is not simply connected
$[t]\mapsto(\cos 2\pi t,\sin 2\pi t)$ is a homeomorphism from $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ to the unit circle
The trigonometric loops give $\pi_1(\{(x,y):x^2+y^2=1\},(1,0))\cong\mathbb Z$
An interval of length one need not embed under $p:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$
A loop that traverses the circle once and then pauses is homotopic to the standard loop
A surjective circle loop can have degree zero and be nullhomotopic
The geometric loops $t\mapsto(\cos 2\pi nt,\sin 2\pi nt)$ have degree $n$
Based circle loops with the same endpoints need not be path-homotopic
A covering quotient of a simply connected space need not be simply connected
FALSE: every continuous self-map of the circle is nullhomotopic
